title: Combination Sum
statement: Return every unique combination of `candidates` that sums to `target`. The same number may be chosen unlimited times. Combinations are sets of choices, so order does not matter. Sort each combination and sort the list.
hints: Sort the candidates so you can stop when a candidate exceeds the remaining target.
Reuse the current index on the recursive call to allow unlimited copies. Advance the index to move to the next candidate.
Record the path when the remainder hits zero.

approaches.name: Sorted backtracking
approaches.explanation: Prune when the candidate exceeds the remainder.

editorial: This is unbounded knapsack written as search. The start index enforces nondecreasing order, which is what makes [2, 2, 3] and [3, 2, 2] the same combination. Passing i, not i + 1, is the single line that allows reuse.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def combination_sum(candidates: list[int], target: int) -> list[list[int]]:
    candidates = sorted(candidates)
    out: list[list[int]] = []
    path: list[int] = []

    def dfs(start: int, remain: int) -> None:
        if remain == 0:
            out.append(path[:])
            return
        for i in range(start, len(candidates)):
            if candidates[i] > remain:
                break
            path.append(candidates[i])
            dfs(i, remain - candidates[i])
            path.pop()

    dfs(0, target)
    return out
